assertions.name: all_linking_numbers_are_integers
assertions.source: a REAL check, counted per pair per insertion across all 694 words: two closed curves cross an even number of times, so an ODD crossing sum means the accounting is wrong. qou-768r's route-3 pass hit exactly that (lk = -3/2) by resolving an averaged letter to the identity rather than to a crossing sign. An earlier draft of this assertion was VACUOUS -- the counter was never incremented -- and is fixed here rather than shipped.

description: EXPLORATORY. Route 3's result rests on a premise true only for MONOTONE words: each summand of the connected-sum closure touches at most 2 components. Sibling #6561 proves the cyclic square (g_m g_{m+1})^2 is the ONLY non-monotone shape yielding a Markov-trace cross term, making it the natural candidate to break that premise. It DOES: measured, it spans 3 distinct components in 188 of 694 insertions -- so the tempting reading that it is local knotting on one component (its closure T(3,2) is a knot) is WRONG. CORRECTED 2026-09-04 -- the original reading, that the conclusion survives for a different reason: in ALL 188 cases at least one pairwise linking number among the three spanned components is nonzero, so Delta != 0 and mubar is not a genuine integer there anyway. The insertion that joins three components is the same one that links them -- IS RETRACTED. Delta != 0 means mubar lives in Z/Delta, NOT that there is no obstruction; a nonzero residue is a nonvanishing invariant. This probe never computed mubar. It is nonzero in 2 of these 188 all-positive spanning insertions, at Delta = 2 with mubar = 1 -- exactly route 3's one-bit residual. See mixed_sign_cyclic_square_does_reopen_milnor_probe.py, which also sweeps all 16 inserted-sign patterns (563 of 3008 nonzero) and re-measures the UNPERTURBED carrier as a control (294 triples, 0 nonzero), so route 3 at Delta = 0 and its Lean are untouched. Scope (a), narrow: one shape, all-positive inserted crossings, sampled word positions, 4 isotopes. NOT a proof that no non-monotone word reopens route 3, and the Delta = 2 one-bit triples are untouched. Nothing wired.

what_is_being_tested.route_3_premise: each summand touches at most 2 components -- TRUE FOR MONOTONE WORDS, which is how the closure decomposes as #_g T(2, e_g)
what_is_being_tested.the_candidate: the cyclic square (g_m g_{m+1})^2, which #6561's RevisitClassCrossTerm.lean shows is the ONLY non-monotone shape producing a trace cross term. It spans THREE strands.
what_is_being_tested.my_wrong_guess: that it would be local knotting on one component, since its closure T(3,2) is a knot and local knotting changes no Milnor invariant. Measured: it spans up to 3 DISTINCT components. Recorded because the guess was reasonable and wrong.
what_is_being_tested.insertion_positions: sampled across the word, not only appended -- braid letters do not commute, so an append-only test would be a weaker claim than it looks

the_result.reading: the premise really does break -- but in every spanning case at least one pairwise linking number is nonzero, so Delta != 0 and mubar is not a genuine integer there. Route 3's PREMISE is monotone-specific and does break; route 3's CONCLUSION ALSO FAILS on this shape, at Delta = 2 -- see the RETRACTED note above and mixed_sign_cyclic_square_does_reopen_milnor_probe.py.

what_this_does_NOT_establish.other_non_monotone_words: NOT tested. This is one shape -- the one #6561 singles out -- not the non-monotone class
what_this_does_NOT_establish.delta_2_triples: NOT examined; still route 3's stated residual
what_this_does_NOT_establish.sign_choices: inserted crossings are all positive. A mixed-sign insertion could cancel a linking number and is not covered
what_this_does_NOT_establish.the_lean: unchanged. MilnorTriplesAreDefinedExactlyWhereTheyVanish.lean proves what it proves; this measures the reach of its hypothesis
